label: Promos
blurb: Short and tightly cut: one message, a browser frame on a backdrop, music.

items.title: 草料二维码：网址一贴，马上出码
items.request: 给草料二维码（https://cli.im/）做一个简短的中文宣传视频：输入一个网址，马上生成二维码，还可以美化一下样式。用于官网首页和社交媒体。中文字幕和中文配音。

items.title: Sketch a diagram in seconds
items.request: Make a short promo video of Excalidraw (https://excalidraw.com), the hand-drawn style whiteboard — show how quickly you can sketch a little diagram (a couple of shapes, an arrow, some text). For a landing page / social post.

items.title: JSON Crack: paste JSON, see the graph
items.request: Make a short promo video of JSON Crack's editor (https://jsoncrack.com/editor): paste a bit of JSON and watch it turn into an interactive graph you can explore. For a landing page / social post.

items.title: Squoosh: shrink images right in your browser
items.request: Make a short promo video of Squoosh (https://squoosh.app), Google's in-browser image compressor — show how it shrinks an image while you compare before/after. For a landing page / social post.

label: Tutorials
blurb: Paced to follow along: one narrated action per step, the camera following each click, a second example, a recap.

items.title: Protein BLAST (blastp) for new lab members
items.request: Make a tutorial video for new lab members on how to use NCBI protein BLAST (blastp): paste a query sequence, choose the database, run it, and read the results (hits table, what E-value / identity mean, opening one alignment). Use human hemoglobin beta as the main example, then show a second example with human insulin so they see how results differ.

items.title: How to find a clinical trial on ClinicalTrials.gov
items.request: Make a tutorial video for patients and caregivers on how to find a clinical trial on ClinicalTrials.gov (https://clinicaltrials.gov): search for a condition near where you live, keep only studies that are recruiting, open one study, and understand the key parts of the study page: what's being tested, who can join (eligibility), where it runs and who to contact. Plain language, no jargon, calm pace.

items.title: Plot a function, add a slider, read off points
items.request: Make a tutorial video for students who have never used Desmos (https://www.desmos.com/calculator): how to plot a function, add a slider to change a parameter, and read off points like intercepts. Use y = a·sin(x) as the example, then a second example like a parabola so they see the same steps work for any function.

items.title: Draw a flowchart, connect, label and export
items.request: Make a tutorial video for new hires who've never used diagrams.net (https://app.diagrams.net): how to start a blank diagram, add a few flowchart shapes, connect them, label them, and export the result as PNG. Then a second quick example (e.g. a decision diamond with yes/no branches) so they see the same steps work for any diagram.

items.title: Your first data analysis in JupyterLite
items.request: Make a tutorial video showing a first data analysis in JupyterLite (https://jupyter.org/try-jupyter/lab/), Jupyter that runs entirely in the browser, nothing to install: open a new Python notebook, load a small dataset with pandas, look at it, compute a summary, and make a chart. For students who have never used Jupyter.

label: Lessons
blurb: Explain the why: concept cards, the idea shown live, a question to check understanding.

items.title: Slope and y-intercept: what m and b mean in y = mx + b
items.request: Make a short lesson video with the Desmos graphing calculator (https://www.desmos.com/calculator) on what m and b mean in y = mx + b (slope and y-intercept), in three languages: English, Simplified Chinese and Spanish, so I can share it with students who speak each one. Same lesson, each fully in its own language: the Desmos interface too, not only the narration.

items.title: Pendiente y ordenada al origen: qué significan m y b en y = mx + b
items.request: Make a short lesson video with the Desmos graphing calculator (https://www.desmos.com/calculator) on what m and b mean in y = mx + b (slope and y-intercept), in three languages: English, Simplified Chinese and Spanish, so I can share it with students who speak each one. Same lesson, each fully in its own language: the Desmos interface too, not only the narration.

items.title: 斜率与 y 轴截距：y = mx + b 中 m 和 b 的含义
items.request: Make a short lesson video with the Desmos graphing calculator (https://www.desmos.com/calculator) on what m and b mean in y = mx + b (slope and y-intercept), in three languages: English, Simplified Chinese and Spanish, so I can share it with students who speak each one. Same lesson, each fully in its own language: the Desmos interface too, not only the narration.

items.title: 二次函数顶点式：a、h、k 怎样改变图像
items.request: 用 GeoGebra 中文版（https://www.geogebra.org/graphing?lang=zh_CN）做一节中文微课：讲清楚二次函数顶点式 y = a(x−h)² + k 里 a、h、k 分别怎么影响图像，为什么。要现场演示（拖动滑动条看变化），中间加一个小测验题让学生先想一想，最后总结。中文字幕和中文配音。

items.title: Git merge vs. rebase, live in Learn Git Branching
items.request: Make a short lesson video using Learn Git Branching (https://learngitbranching.js.org/) that explains the difference between git merge and git rebase: start from the same two branches, show what merge does to the history, then what rebase does, and when you'd pick each. For developers who use git daily but never really got rebase.

items.title: Why hemoglobin has four chains and four hemes
items.request: Make a short lesson video on protein structure using hemoglobin (PDB 4HHB) on RCSB PDB (start at https://www.rcsb.org/structure/4HHB, and use its 3D viewer). Explain WHY hemoglobin is built the way it is: four chains (two alpha, two beta), each holding a heme group that binds oxygen. Show where to find this on the entry page and in the 3D view. Include a quick check-your-understanding question.

items.title: How regular expressions match: literals, \d, + and {3}
items.request: Make a short lesson video that explains how regular expressions match text, using regex101 (https://regex101.com) to show it live: literal characters, character classes like \d, and quantifiers like + and {3}. I want students to understand WHY a pattern matches or not, not just click buttons. A quick check-your-understanding question would be great.

items.title: How Dijkstra Finds Shortest Paths
items.request: Make a short lesson video that makes a hard algorithm idea visible, using VisuAlgo (https://visualgo.net). For example, why merge sort is faster than insertion sort on a large shuffled array, or how Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths. For first-year CS students.

label: Help-center docs
blurb: Per-step GIFs and screenshots cropped to the action, plus a ready-to-paste article.

items.title: Filter a table, add a facet, export CSV
items.site: Datasette (local copy of the public demo)
items.request: We need help-center GIFs and a short article for Datasette: how to filter a table, use a facet, and export the filtered rows as CSV. Use the public demo at https://global-power-plants.datasettes.com/global-power-plants/global-power-plants (e.g. show only solar plants in one country).

items.title: Export a drawing as PNG (transparent or white)
items.request: We need help-center GIFs and a short article for Excalidraw (https://excalidraw.com): how to export your drawing as a PNG image — including choosing a transparent or white background — and how to copy it to the clipboard. Draw something tiny first so there's something to export.

items.title: Create, edit and export a flowchart in Mermaid Live Editor
items.request: We need help-center GIFs and a short article for Mermaid Live Editor (https://mermaid.live): how to start a flowchart from the sample, edit the text to add a node, and export the diagram as an SVG or PNG.
